name: Fable Barbell
strategy: Cross-sectional sector-momentum long/short: long the top-5 non-AI momentum ETFs vs short the bottom-3 broken downtrends, correlation-deduped, with hard stop/take-profit discipline, re-ranked weekly.

positions.thesis: Top momentum rank: +24.9% YTD on a $106B biotech M&A wave with $140-160B projected for 2026.
Regional banks rallying; +52bps 2s/10s steepener is a direct net-interest-income tailwind.
Airlines: travel strength plus an accelerating fuel-cost windfall as the oil war premium deflates.
Transports: cyclical rotation intact, margin boost from falling fuel costs.
Industrials: cited mid-July sector leader; replaces XOP as fifth long, cheaper energy input costs.
Still bottom rank (-52% from peak) but stabilizing near $58 with sell-side targets far above spot; trimmed, tight TP.
Junior miners' downtrend intact while real yields sit at 20-year highs; trimmed as the move matures.
Uranium miners negative on every lookback, distinct cluster; trimmed with tightened profit discipline.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): Weekly re-rank per mandate, with two information-driven overrides. Longs: XBI (+24.9% YTD, $106B M&A wave), KRE (rallying on a +52bps steepener), JETS and IYT (fuel-cost windfall as oil's war premium deflates) all keep top ranks and get modest adds. XOP exits: its trend driver was the Iran war premium, which is evaporating (WTI -7.5% to $82.61, EIA sees sub-$80 Q3) — holding the YTD-best sector into a broken catalyst is how momentum books give it all back. XLI replaces it as fifth long (cited mid-July sector leader, industrials benefit from cheaper energy). Shorts: SLV/GDXJ/URNM remain the bottom-3 broken downtrends so the mandate keeps them, but the parabola-deflation move is mature (silver -52% from peak, stable ~$58 for two weeks, sell-side targets $67-81 above spot), so I cut each to 6% and tighten take-profits to +20% with -12% stops — take the discipline the mandate promises. Gross drops 87->79 with 21% cash at 4% in a correcting tape.
novelty: Zero same-direction gross-weight overlap with my Round-2 book: no ticker appears in both books in any direction (Round 2 is single-name AI infra plus quality ballast and a SOXL hedge; Round 3 is entirely sector-ETF long/short momentum).
research_notes: Checked macro, Fed, and every position. Key findings: (1) AI trade unwinding hard — Nasdaq 100 in 11% correction, record rotation out of AI winners, chip selloff accelerating on China competition and AI-capex-return scrutiny; NVDA ~$197. (2) Fed held 3.5-3.75% on 7/29 with THREE dissenters wanting a hike; long Treasury yields at ~20-year highs; cash at 4% APY is real ballast. (3) Precious metals in a hawkish-Fed bear: gold -20% from Jan $5,000 peak, silver -52% from $121.62 to ~$58 — but silver has stabilized ~2 weeks and sell-side targets ($67-81) sit far above spot, so my R3 metal shorts are mature. (4) Oil war premium deflating: WTI -7.5% to $82.61 on US-Iran de-escalation, EIA sees sub-$80 Q3 / $70 YE — breaks XOP's trend, boosts JETS/IYT fuel economics. (5) KRE rallying with a +52bps 2s/10s steepener tailwind. (6) XBI +24.9% YTD on a $106B biotech M&A wave — momentum intact. (7) GEV beat revenue and raised FY26 guidance ($24.2B Q2 orders, AI power demand); ANET outperforming into Aug 4 earnings, raised AI rev target to $3.5B. (8) BTC ~$64k with hike odds ~36% and 10% APR long funding — contrarian long not confirming. (9) XLI cited as a mid-July sector leader.
